extracted.intended_audience: aspiring essayists and poets interested in experimenting with lyric essays / creative nonfiction
extracted.subtask_description: A workshop-style syllabus for writing lyric essays — hybrid pieces of creative nonfiction that use poetic techniques (juxtaposition, collage, white space, sound, associative thinking) and experiment with forms such as braided and hermit-crab essays. The course mixes reading models, guided exercises, peer/instructor review, and two graded submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment with form / flexible genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with form and explore the possibilities of this flexible genre; work exists in a liminal space that touches on the poetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed with an attitude of play, openness, and communal exploration; reach for your own definitions and methods while studying others for models and inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques: juxtaposition, collage, white space, sound, associative thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use techniques such as juxtaposition; collage; white space; attention to sound; and loose, associative thinking that move nonfiction in ways often associated with poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these techniques in exercises and drafts (Week 1 focuses on collage and white space). These elements help lyric essays 'move' like poetry rather than following strictly linear exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Braided essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Build pieces that braid multiple threads — thematic or narrative strands woven together (the 'braided essay').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Week 2 builds on collage and white space to examine braided forms; students will experiment with braided pieces and turn in the first assignment using this model as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermit crab essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct essays that 'sneak' personal narrative into other forms (e.g., a job letter, shopping list, how-to manual) — the hermit crab essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine examples of hermit crab essays and experiment by writing personal content inside nontraditional forms; Week 2 includes practice and assignment opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyric vignette and prose poem qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ prose-poem and vignette techniques to capture emotional truths using juxtaposition, hyperbole, and absurd or surreal leaps of logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how lyrical vignettes can remain true to events while employing dreamlike or absurd qualities to communicate wonder and mystery (Week 3 focus). Use these devices intentionally to balance lyricism with factual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnessing the self / essays by poets
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate the poet-as-witness stance in personal essay: being temporarily emptied of personality yet connected to a self (the 'gazer'), attending to moments of connection and disconnection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study essays by poets (e.g., Ross Gay, Lucia Perillo, Amy Gerstler, Elizabeth Bishop) and use guided exercises to find and craft moments of witnessing and self-observation in your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid forms & documentary impulse
rubrics_metrics.description: Straddle and combine genres, exploring multimedia work and 'documentary poetics' that observe social life and collect text, images, and observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look to writers and artists such as Claudia Rankine, Bernadette Mayer, Roz Chast, and Maira Kalman for models; experiment with multimedia/documentary approaches and incorporate collected material as part of the final project (Week 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and study contemporary models
rubrics_metrics.description: Read contemporary pieces that straddle the line between personal essay and poem (e.g., Toi Derricotte, Anne Carson, Maggie Nelson) to inform your practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assigned readings as models and inspiration; analyze how other writers use form, voice, and technique to create lyric essays and adapt lessons to your own experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments: two essay submissions with specified lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity to submit two essays of 1000 and 2500 words each for instructor and/or peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some weeks include submission windows for these essays (first assignment around Week 2; final essay due near end of course). Use peer and instructor feedback to revise and develop work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly participation for feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are expected to participate weekly in class discussions to receive instructor feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular engagement in discussions improves classroom experience for all and is necessary to receive instructor feedback; apart from one optional live conference, there is no requirement to be online at set times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional exercises and synchronous opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Some weeks include additional optional writing exercises and an optional video conference that is open to all students (recorded for later viewing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take advantage of optional exercises to deepen experimentation and review recorded video conferences if you cannot attend live; these are supplementary to the core readings and assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude and workshop ethos
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach the work with playfulness, openness, and communal exploration, aiming to 'reach for our own definitions and methods' while learning from others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize experimentation over strict adherence to rules; value risk-taking and model study while using peer/instructor feedback to refine your unique approach to lyric nonfiction.
